clue.text: Female Greek athlete originally seen in US Olympic city

indicators.note: something seen in a place is inside it, so one letter goes within the city's name

parts.note: Atlanta hosted the 1996 Summer Olympics

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the word athlete, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A Greek sportswoman first spotted competing at the Atlanta Games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'athlete' seems to belong with 'Female Greek' in the definition, but 'originally' takes only its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Atalanta was a swift huntress who raced her suitors, a female heroine famed for running.

clue.text: Large revolver protects the entertainers

parts.note: large means big
a top is a toy that spins, so it revolves

explanation.surface: A big gun is guarding the performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolver' suggests a pistol, but it is a spinning toy. The definition is descriptive: the big top is the circus tent that shelters the performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A big top is the large circus tent, the covering under which circus performers do their acts.

clue.text: Change at Naples for Nice

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of these letters

explanation.surface: A traveller switches trains at Naples to reach Nice on the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice reads as the French city, matching Naples, but it is the adjective. Rearranging AT NAPLES gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice and pleasant are synonyms, both meaning agreeable or enjoyable.

clue.text: Position in which man takes notes

indicators.note: a man taking something gains it after his name, so the pieces join end to end

parts.note: Stan is a man's name
C and E are musical notes

explanation.surface: A stance in which a man jots down notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a way of standing or a stated view, both senses of a position.

clue.text: A kiss in a love story, say, makes a neat ending

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter

indicators.note: say signals that the word is pronounced, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: a story is a tale

explanation.surface: A romantic novel's kiss provides a tidy conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like the adjective tidy, but it is the old word for cattle, so the tail of an ox is a neat's ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an archaic word for cattle, so the tail of an ox is literally the end of a neat.

clue.text: Present for next door

definitions.meaning: present means available, here and ready
next door means very close by, within reach

explanation.definitionFit: On hand means available and nearby, matching both present and close by.

clue.text: Unwilling to be clad in Anglican dress

indicators.note: something clad in clothing is wrapped by it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: CE is short for Church of England, the Anglican church
loth means unwilling or reluctant

explanation.surface: A reluctant cleric must wear Anglican vestments.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress someone is to put garments on them, the verb sense of clothe.

clue.text: Tracts of eastern and southern states

parts.note: states as a verb means says

explanation.surface: Pamphlets about the eastern and southern US states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'states' reads as the regions of a country, but it is the verb meaning declares.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short written treatise, so tracts are short pieces of writing like essays.

clue.text: Girl arrives drunk at year celebration

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and jumbled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A tipsy girl turns up at a year-end party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' acts on 'arrives' alone, giving IVERSAR; 'at' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An anniversary is a yearly commemoration, a celebration of a past date.

clue.text: Fifty entering card game at the same time

indicators.note: entering means going into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: whist is a card game for four players
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty people join a whist drive simultaneously.
explanation.definitionFit: Whilst means while, during the time that something else happens.

clue.text: Sean sent new order

indicators.note: new signals that the letters take a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Sean dispatched a fresh request to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a purchase, but it means tidiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Order in the sense of tidy arrangement is a synonym of neatness.

clue.text: Article on name-dropping

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A gossip column piece about celebrities being mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'name-dropping' suggests boasting of famous friends, but it means with the name left off, as in anonymous.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is short for anonymous, describing a work whose author's name has been dropped.

clue.text: Detective magazine

definitions.meaning: a detective here is a hired sleuth not in the police
a magazine here is the British satirical fortnightly of that title

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a hired investigator and is also the name of a British satirical magazine.

clue.text: They go ahead to walk the dogs

parts.note: to pace is to walk steadily
setters are breeds of gun dog

explanation.surface: Someone sets off to exercise the dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walk the dogs' reads as one chore, but splits into a verb and a breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacesetters lead the way in a race or field, those who go in front of others.

clue.text: Sense there's agreement among a number

indicators.note: among means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: eight is a number
yes is a word of agreement

explanation.surface: A sense of consensus among a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of vision, one of the five senses.

clue.text: Watch salesman meets consumer

parts.note: rep is short for a sales representative
an eater consumes food

explanation.surface: A watch salesman meets a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a repeater is a watch that chimes the hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeater is a watch that strikes the last hour or quarter when a spring is pressed.

clue.text: Come to a hill

parts.note: a mount is a hill, as in names like Mount Everest

explanation.definitionFit: To amount to is to come to a total, as a bill comes to a sum.

clue.text: Signs liable to be kicked over

definitions.meaning: signs here means marks or vestiges left behind
to kick over the harness straps is an idiom for throwing off restraint

explanation.definitionFit: Traces are vestiges left behind, and also the straps of a harness in the idiom kick over the traces.

clue.text: Secretary uses one name, Susan, for disguise

indicators.note: a disguise changes the look of something, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A secretary goes incognito under the name Susan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uses' is only a link; the fodder is I (one), NAME and SUSAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis is a person employed to write from dictation, a literary secretary.

clue.text: Required study about river that's rising

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means read from bottom to top, backwards
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for work
the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: Research needed on a river whose waters are going up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's rising' suits a down entry, read upwards; the container made first is DEDEEN. The Dee is a river in Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: Needed and required are synonyms, both meaning necessary.

clue.text: The sound of a swan or seal

indicators.note: the sound of tells us to take a word that is pronounced alike

parts.note: a cygnet is a young swan

explanation.surface: A noise made by a swan or a seal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seal' reads as the animal, paired with the swan, but it is a stamp for sealing documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A signet is a small seal, often set in a ring, used to stamp documents.

clue.text: Cheer up with a fringe benefit

definitions.meaning: to cheer up is to brighten or liven, with up
a fringe benefit is an extra advantage given with a job

explanation.definitionFit: Perk up means brighten, and a perk is a perquisite or job benefit.

clue.text: The mother of all lakes?

parts.note: a nun heading a convent bears this title after Mother, and it is also the name of the largest North American Great Lake

explanation.definitionFit: Lake Superior is the largest of the Great Lakes, and Mother Superior is a convent's head.

clue.text: Not only on the cricket field will it go to fine leg

definitions.text: Not only on the cricket field will it go to fine leg

parts.words: Not only on the cricket field will it go to fine leg
parts.note: a deflecting stroke sends the ball toward fine leg in cricket, and elsewhere a quick look can fall on a shapely leg

explanation.definitionFit: A glance is a brief look and also a cricket stroke angling the ball fine on the leg side.

clue.text: Produce nippers

parts.note: nippers suggests children, but here it means the little biting things that come through a baby's gums

explanation.definitionFit: Teething is when a baby's first teeth come through, so the verb means producing them.

clue.text: A break in the depression

definitions.meaning: a break here is a pause or interval, as in Parliament
depression here is a hollow or alcove set into a wall

explanation.definitionFit: A recess is an adjournment or holiday, and also a niche or indentation in a surface.
